target.title: Jointly Learning Visual and Auditory Speech Representations from Raw Data

entries.text: RA VEn jointly learns visual and auditory speech representations in a single self-supervised pre-training stage from raw video and audio.
entries.condition: Pre-training; no transcript labels or handcrafted audio/video targets are used for the representation-learning objective.
entries.quote:
In this paper, we present a single-stage self-supervised approach that jointly learns visual and au-
ditory speech representations from raw video and audio only.

entries.text: The asymmetric objective has the audio student predict both video and audio teacher targets, while the video student predicts only audio targets.
entries.condition: Cross-modal losses cover all time positions; the audio-to-audio within-modal loss covers masked positions only.
entries.quote:
Namely, while the audio
student predicts outputs from both video and audio teachers (cross- and within-modal learning), the
video student predicts only auditory targets (cross-modal learning).

entries.text: The authors present momentum teachers and masked prediction as eliminating the need for handcrafted targets or multi-stage pre-training.
entries.condition: Self-supervised pre-training of visual and audio encoders.

entries.text: Teacher parameters are updated by an exponential moving average with a cosine-scheduled momentum from 0.999 to 1.
entries.condition: Applied at every pre-training iteration to modality-specific teachers; teacher architecture matches its student encoder.

entries.text: Video inputs are grayscale mouth-region clips; audio is sampled at 16 kHz and features are produced at 25 frames per second.
entries.condition: The video/audio temporal sampling rates are aligned; the paper's preprocessing crops a 96×96 mouth-centered region and splits utterances longer than 24 seconds.

entries.text: The pre-training mask start probability is 0.2 and a selected video start masks three consecutive frames, corresponding to 1,920 audio samples.
entries.condition: Masking ablation selects probability 0.2 and length 3; audio masking is enlarged by 640 at 16 kHz versus 25 fps.

entries.text: The Base and Large temporal encoders have 12 and 24 Transformer blocks and 41 million and 328 million parameters, respectively.
entries.condition: Base hidden/MLP/head sizes are 512/2048/8; Large sizes are 1024/4096/16.

entries.text: Low-resource fine-tuning uses 30 labelled hours from LRS3 trainval; high-resource fine-tuning uses the full 433-hour LRS3 dataset.
entries.condition: Low-resource and high-resource settings respectively; LRS3 test set is used for reported results.

entries.text: Self-training first fine-tunes the pre-trained audio encoder on labelled data, pseudo-labels unlabelled data, and then fine-tunes the pre-trained video and audio models on both label types.
entries.condition: For the low-resource headline results, the labelled set is 30 hours of LRS3; authors say self-training requires no extra data.

entries.text: Fine-tuning uses joint CTC/attention decoding, CTC weight 0.1, and SentencePiece subword targets with vocabulary size 1,000.
entries.condition: Applies to VSR and ASR fine-tuning; the target token vocabulary is SentencePiece.

entries.text: Decoding uses beam size 40; the language-model fusion weight is selected from 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, or 0.4 on a validation set.
entries.condition: LM score is optional and added by shallow fusion; the paper does not identify the validation split here.

entries.text: The authors claim RA VEn exceeds all related methods on VSR in the 30-hour LRS3 low-resource setting and improves over AV-HuBERT Base by 4.8 or 5.9 WER points depending on pre-training data.
entries.condition: LRS3 test; 30 labelled hours; Base models; RA VEn versus AV-HuBERT Base with 433 or 1,759 unlabelled pre-training hours, respectively.
entries.quote: It surpasses the Base A V-HuBERT model by 4.8% and 5.9% WER when using LRS3 and LRS3+V ox2-en, respectively, despite having roughly half the number of parameters.

entries.text: RA VEn Base achieves VSR/ASR WER 47.0%/4.7%.
entries.condition: LRS3 test; Base; pre-trained on 433 hours of unlabelled LRS3; fine-tuned on 30 labelled LRS3 trainval hours; no LM.

entries.text: The from-scratch video-to-speech synthesis baseline reports PESQ/STOI/ESTOI 1.26/0.53/0.30.

entries.condition: LRS3 test; SVTS Transformer; video encoder initialized from the RA VEn Large model pre-trained on LRS3+VoxCeleb2-en; 30 epochs with learning rate 2×10−4.

entries.text: The authors report pre-training gains of 0.04 PESQ, 0.03 STOI, and 0.06 ESTOI, larger than gains attributed to a roughly fourfold larger training set in Mira et al. (2022).
entries.unit: metric-point gains (PESQ / STOI / ESTOI); training-set size factor
entries.condition: Video-to-speech synthesis on LRS3 test; RA VEn initialization versus SVTS trained from scratch; compared with Mira et al. LRS3 versus LRS3+Vox2-en.

entries.text: Pre-training uses 32 A100 GPUs for Base and 128 A100 GPUs for Large; reported epoch times are about 15 minutes to 2 hours depending on model and data.
entries.unit: A100 GPUs; hours per epoch (conditions specified in text)
entries.condition: Base on LRS3: about 15 minutes/epoch; Base on LRS3+Vox2-en: about 1 hour/epoch; Large on LRS3+Vox2-en: about 2 hours/epoch.

entries.text: Single-GPU inference without batching takes about 3 seconds to decode 10 seconds of footage for Base and 5 seconds for Large.
entries.condition: One A100 GPU; no batching; Base and Large respectively.

entries.text: The authors acknowledge surveillance/privacy misuse and possible demographic performance disparities from under-represented groups in training data.
entries.condition: Ethics statement; risks discussed for lipreading technology and datasets with possible gender, age, or ethnic imbalance.

entries.text: The authors identify weight sharing between visual and audio encoders and transfer to other speech tasks as future work, not demonstrated results.
entries.condition: Conclusion; weight sharing is proposed to reduce pre-training memory requirements.

entries.text: The paper does not report random seeds or repeated-run counts/variance for the headline evaluation results.
entries.condition: Applies to reported LRS3/LRS2 test WER and ablations; training and evaluation variability is not quantified in the paper.
entries.quote: To ensure reproducibility, we provide as many implementation details as possible in the main paper as well as tables showing the hyperparameter values in the appendix.

entries.text: Although LRS3 test speakers are said to be separate from speakers in the training set, the paper does not specify whether test speakers or clips were excluded from unlabelled self-supervised pre-training on LRS3.
entries.condition: LRS3 test versus the unlabelled LRS3 component of pre-training; speaker overlap and exact exclusion policy are not specified.

entries.text: The paper does not identify the exact validation examples/speakers or selection procedure used for LM-weight tuning; the ablation validation set is attributed to Shi et al. without its membership being described.
entries.condition: Relevant to decoding LM fusion weight and ablation/model choices; paper says a validation set is used but does not specify exact partition membership or whether all selection used it.

entries.text: No chance-level or other random-recognition reference is reported for WER evaluation.
entries.condition: LRS3 and LRS2 recognition test results; chance is not operationally defined for the unconstrained-vocabulary WER task.
entries.loc: Table 1 caption; Table 2 caption; Appendix B

entries.text: LRS2 test-set duration, speaker separation from training/pre-training, and evaluation speaker counts are not specified, although Table 9 reports test-set results.
entries.condition: LRS2 benchmark; the appendix describes thousands of diverse speakers and 223 labelled hours but gives no test-subset speaker accounting.

entries.text: The paper specifies grayscale mouth crops but not the video intensity normalization mean and standard deviation used by the public evaluation implementation.
entries.condition: Input preprocessing; code reports channel mean 0.421 and standard deviation 0.165.

entries.text: The paper gives low- and high-resource labelled-hour totals but not a complete manifest of examples or speaker composition for the trainval subset and validation set.
entries.condition: LRS3 supervised fine-tuning and model selection; trainval is named, but item-level inclusion and speaker composition are not described.

entries.text: The source, filtering, confidence thresholds, and exact data partition used for self-training pseudo-labels are not fully stated.
entries.condition: Self-training stage; paper says unlabelled data are pseudo-labelled and no extra data are required, but does not document pseudo-label selection/filtering details.
entries.quote:
we do not require extra
data for the self-training phase.

entries.text: The public test harness fixes the evaluation seed at 42 with worker seeding enabled; the paper does not report an evaluation seed.
entries.condition: Evaluation harness only; this does not establish the seed(s) used for paper training runs.

entries.text: The public evaluation transform divides video pixels by 255, converts to grayscale, center-crops to 88×88 at test time, and normalizes with mean 0.421 and standard deviation 0.165; these normalization constants are not stated in the paper.
entries.unit: pixels; grayscale mean; grayscale standard deviation
entries.condition: Test/validation transform in the public code; paper states mouth crop/grayscale but not these evaluation normalization values or center-crop operation.

entries.text: The public low-resource Large self-training-plus-LM test scripts set the decoding LM weight to 0.3; the paper lists candidate weights but not the selected value.
entries.condition: LRS3 trainval test scripts for both VSR and ASR; scripts load the listed LM checkpoint and use the low-resource test manifest.
entries.quote: When using a language model,β is chosen from{0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4} using the validation set.

entries.text: The public waveform loader calls torchaudio.load with normalize=True, which converts/scales encoded audio to floating point; the paper describes raw audio without preprocessing or normalization.
entries.condition: Observed in the public evaluation data loader; this is a loader-level audio conversion/scaling setting and the paper does not describe it.

entries.text: The public test configuration reads an explicit test CSV; the low-resource dataset config names separate trainval, validation, and test CSV manifests.
entries.condition: Code maps lrs3_trainval.yaml test_csv to test_with_tags_counts_unigram1000.csv and validation to val_with_tags_counts_unigram1000.csv; exact manifest membership is not documented in the paper.

entries.text: The authors explicitly warn that lipreading can be misused for surveillance and thereby compromise public privacy and trust.
entries.condition: Ethics statement; the paper notes improving CCTV may exacerbate this concern.

entries.text: LRS3 has a vocabulary exceeding 50,000 words and thousands of speakers; its test set is about 1 hour and is speaker-disjoint from the training set.
entries.condition: LRS3 benchmark; the paper describes test speakers as separate from training speakers but does not clarify overlap with unlabelled pre-training.

questions.q: What is the paper's central methodological contribution?
questions.answer: A single-stage self-supervised method jointly learns audio and visual speech encoders from raw synchronized streams, using masked student inputs, momentum-teacher targets, and an asymmetric prediction objective: audio predicts both modalities while video predicts audio only.

questions.q: What performance claims are best supported by the reported headline results?
questions.answer: For LRS3 low-resource VSR, the best reported RA VEn result is 23.8% WER with Large, self-training, and an LM on 30 labelled hours; for high-resource VSR it is 23.1% on 433 labelled hours. High-resource ASR is 1.4% WER. The paper reports consistent VSR gains over AV-HuBERT, while the 1.4% ASR result is described as on par with state of the art.

questions.q: What qualifications should accompany those comparisons?
questions.answer: The results are test-set WER values with different labeled and unlabelled data budgets; the paper reports no repeated-run variance, leaves LRS3 pre-training/test speaker overlap and selection-set membership unclear, and does not test noisy-audio audiovisual recognition. The public test code also specifies an evaluation seed, video normalization values, and a selected LM weight absent from the paper.

questions.q: What caveats and future-work boundaries do the authors explicitly acknowledge?
questions.answer: They note privacy/surveillance and dataset-bias risks, leave noisy-audio audiovisual evaluation for future work, and identify encoder weight sharing and transfer to other speech tasks as future directions.
